properties.research_architect: Robert Alexander Kennard and Robert Marks / Kennard
properties.research_topics: Zeiger; Kennard; Marks; shallow pools; stepping stones; project index; date distinction; Kimmelman; 1966 directory; community meetings; 1960; party; date uncertain
properties.research_summary: Irving Zeiger’s single-story wood-frame Ranch-style flag-lot house was designed by Robert Alexander Kennard and partner Robert Marks and landscaped by Eckbo in 1958; designated Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument 1083 in March 2015. Article describes trellised patios, shallow tiled fountain pools, round aggregate stepping pavers and a swimming pool. Project index lists Irving Zeiger, Los Angeles, job 1849, date 1957, Kennard architect. This is an archival project date and should be kept separate from the 1958 landscape date in Simon and the workbook’s 1959 building date.

properties.research_topics: postwar modernism; studio; half acre; Alcoa; aluminum; trellis; post and beam; fountain; construction chronology; carport; address verified; lot 60; garden plan; unbuilt designs; design phases; 1957 plan; Alcoa chronology; 1956 proposal; 1957 drawings; 1959 construction; solar control; microclimate; screens; pavilion; aluminum fountain; mixed materials; historical condition; preservation; loss of aluminum garden; 1996 visit; Eckbo; master tree plan; 1953
properties.research_summary: Josef van der Kar designed Eckbo’s own house, described as a 1953 house in the caption; half-acre lot, about two-thirds level, reached by a 150-foot rising driveway; 1,500-square-foot house and 800-square-foot studio under one sloping roof. Photo caption dates trellis and screens to 1955 and describes the aluminum structures as Alcoa demonstration structures. Simon dates the single-story post-and-beam house designed by Josef Van Der Kar to 1952; the garden became an ALCOA Forecast Garden. She dates an ALCOA commission to 1959 and describes an abstract open-flower fountain and perforated aluminum overhead structures. Treib dates construction of the van der Kar-designed Eckbo house to 1951 and occupancy to 1952. His description gives approximately 1,500 square feet of living space and an 800 square foot studio initially separated by an open carport, later enclosed. The reproduced 24 April 1952 garden plan explicitly labels lot 60, tract 15007,8942 Wonderland Park Avenue, Los Angeles 46, Mr and Mrs Garrett Eckbo. Address and lot were visually verified in the plan title. Treib distinguishes an ambitious April 1952 garden proposal, a more restrained circa 1954 plan, a signed 12 November 1957 plan and the later ALCOA project; he states that no initial scheme appears to have been executed in its entirety. Treib traces ALCOA project correspondence to 16 October 1956, earliest existing drawings to 30 May 1957, and an agreement to 4 March 1959 before construction. The opening photo caption describes the garden in late 1959 shortly after completion. The garden responded to heat gain on east/south house glazing with aluminum sunbreaks, privacy screens, a freestanding pavilion and an abstract flower-form fountain. Expanded metal created filtered light and varying transparency; wood remained in structural supports and benches. Treib describes renovation consultations in 1987 and 1989 and reports that almost nothing of the original Forecast Garden’s aluminum ensemble remained on his 1996 visit; concrete aggregate paths with ceramic insets and wooden pavilion posts survived. He characterizes the original Forecast Garden as having effectively disappeared before 1988.

properties.research_topics: Rykoff; 1957 revision; step stones; tree rows; 1954–1955; lot 65
properties.research_summary: Richard Rykoff’s triangular narrow-lot garden was designed by Eckbo; original planting plan 1955 and revised plan September 11,1957. Article describes Brisbane box at entry, Cape honeysuckle at street slope, Platanus acerifolia row and Eucalyptus torquata beyond the boundary; revised plan called for redwood rounds and Palos Verdes stone step stones. Project index lists Richard Rykoff at Wonderland Park lot 65, job 1218, date 1954–1955, with manuscript 76|692 and drawing FF 588 references. By-sheet listing gives 1954. These project dates should not replace a house construction date.
